original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Prove that the six-call orbit O5, represented by (0,1,1,1)/(1,1,1) with residual diag(3,2), is character-excluded. The argument uses the quadratic form 3 x1^2 + 2 x2^2 on the coordinate-swapped residual diag(2,3) and transports the exclusion to the four profiles of the orbit.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers the O5 question left open by PR #7128, which is the parity-image test of PR #7035 with the coefficient of x2^2 changed from 1 to 2.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the signed-frame escape. The four profiles still need more than six paid calls, so there is no local call-count saving and no selected-frontier change.
stop_rule: Stop after a character exclusion of O5, a rational decomposition that survives every additive character, or a written obstruction left by the redone 2-adic split. Do not redo O2, and do not take the O3 or O4 support questions.
evidence: Elementary character proof for every rational rank-one solution of R+S+T=diag(2,3): every decomposition has a pair whose parity image misses (1,1), so an AB or PQ form extends and detects two calls and four targets. The bracket, doubled-matrix identities, Cramer determinant, and axis rearrangement are expanded polynomials. Lemma 5 is the 32-class mod-8 check. Two witnesses show that some other pair can have image (1,1); the odd-k axis valuation is not strict. Transport by t, h, and sh carries the exclusion to the four O5 profiles. The inherited call inequality is not reproved. No kappa change.

open_questions.question: Does every decomposition of (2,1,1,0)/(1,1,1) fail a character or fail target support?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR #7128 shows this orbit is not character-excluded. A word, if one exists, has to satisfy target support as well.
open_questions.first_step: Describe the decompositions that pass every character, starting from the lattice Z^3 + Z(1/2,1/2,1/2) of the witness -B + (5/2)Q + (1/4)(1,3)(1,3)^T, and test the subset sums for A+Q on that family.
open_questions.blocked_by: The character test alone cannot close the orbit, and no support classification of that lattice is supplied.

open_questions.question: Does every decomposition of (0,1,1,1)/(1,1,2) fail a character or fail target support?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the other orbit #7128 left open with a character survivor. It is not the six-call orbit settled here: the third multiplicity is 2.
open_questions.first_step: Start from the witness (1/2)B + (1/2)(2,1)(2,1)^T + 2Q and test subset sums for A+P and A+Q on the decompositions that pass every character.
open_questions.blocked_by: No classification of the character-surviving family is supplied.
